newsitem.title: USA: Friendly Flagstar restructuring seen likely.
newsitem.headline: Friendly Flagstar restructuring seen likely.

text.p: A tentative agreement between Flagstar Cos Inc and its various creditors to restructure the struggling restaurant company is likely to be quickly approved by all the parties involved, several Wall Street analysts said.
"This is likely to end with a quick restructuring," said Neal Goldman, a distressed debt analyst at Salomon Brothers Inc.
"The company wanted a quick restructuring process so they were willing to give subordinated bondholders what they wanted. This is a very reasonable plan." he said.
The proposed plan gives 95.5 percent of the stock of the restructured company to holders of $847 million in senior subordinated debentures.
After the announcement, bond investors bid up the Flagstar subordinated bonds almost 10 points from Monday's closing levels of 36-39. The bonds were trading at 45 on Tuesday.

But the good news defied the hopes of some investors who were shorting the subordinated debt. Much of the price increase on the subordinated bonds was generated from investors covering short positions ater the plan was unveiled, traders said.
Wall Street analysts also expected holders of $550 million in senior notes to eventually lend their approval to the restructuring, even though they were not involved in the negotiations.
Under the plan, noteholders will be asked to accept a reduced coupon and extend the maturity of their notes. In exchange, the restructured company would repay all the principal on the senior notes.
Daniel Golden, a lawyer at Stroock & Stroock & Levan who is representing the senior creditors, did not immediately return calls.

"The company will have to offer compensation in exchange from the consent of the senior bondholders," said Barbara Wedelstaedt, an analyst at KDP Investment Advisors. "They'll have to give them warrants, cash or a PIK portion."
She said none of these are options that would have a negative impact on the credit quality or outlook for the restructured company.
Wedelstaedt added, "Even if you keep the bonds unimpared, it's still not a deal-breaker. The company has the money to pay the bonds as they are."

Senior notes closed higher by half a point, at 98.5 after the announcement of the plan. Global hedge-fund manager, George Soros, was rumored to be one of the investors in the senior debt. A spokesman for Soros declined to comment
Flagstar said specifics proposed changes to the senior bonds would be released in an upcoming S-4 filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
Analysts say the restructuring is likely to be carried out via a pre-packaged bankruptcy filing. The entire process could be completed by the summertime, they said.
